sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。
我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantham）。

sentences.en: Democrats were not the only ones chagrined after the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在美国总统大选结束后，感到懊恼的不仅仅是民主党人。

sentences.en: Donald Trump's election has sent shockwaves through the world of pollsters and political analysts.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的当选在民调专家和政治分析人士的世界中引发了巨大震动。

sentences.en: Pundits on both the left and right had predicted Hillary Clinton would walk away with the race.
sentences.zh: 左派和右派的权威人士此前都预测希拉里·克林顿会轻松赢得这场竞选。

sentences.en: Today, we're talking to one expert who got it right.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们采访了一位预测准确的专家。

sentences.en: There are several surprising things about him.
sentences.zh: 关于他，有几件令人惊讶的事情。

sentences.en: For one thing, Alan Lichtman is a historian, not a data scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 首先，艾伦·利希特曼（Alan Lichtman）是一位历史学家，而不是数据科学家。

sentences.en: For another, this wasn't a fluke.
This is the ninth time in a row he's called the election correctly.
sentences.zh: 这是他连续第九次准确预测了大选结果。

sentences.en: Finally, and this is the craziest part, Alan often calls the winner months and sometimes years before an election.
sentences.zh: 最后，也是最疯狂的一点，艾伦往往在大选前几个月，有时甚至是几年前，就能预测出获胜者。

sentences.en: He's sometimes called elections before he knows which candidates are running.
sentences.zh: 他有时甚至在不知道候选人是谁的情况下就预测了大选结果。

sentences.en: Alan says his secret is sitting in plain sight.
sentences.zh: 艾伦说，他的秘诀就摆在显眼的地方。

sentences.en: But most of us are too consumed with the drama of campaigns and candidates to see it.
sentences.zh: 但我们大多数人太沉迷于竞选和候选人的戏码，以至于忽略了它。

sentences.en: Alan Lichtman, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 艾伦·利希特曼，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Alan, you're in the Middle East right now in a hotel room in Qatar.
sentences.zh: 艾伦，你现在身处中东，在卡塔尔的一家酒店房间里。

sentences.en: I want to take you back more than a quarter century.
sentences.zh: 我想带你回到二十五年前。

sentences.en: You were at Caltech and you sat down to dinner next to another academic.
sentences.zh: 当时你在加州理工学院，和另一位学者坐在一起吃晚餐。
你们是一对奇怪的组合。

sentences.en: You're a historian with an interest in American politics.
sentences.zh: 你是一位对美国政治感兴趣的历史学家。
而他是一位地球物理学家。

sentences.en: Since our story begins at that dinner, can you tell me who you sat next to and what you talked about?
sentences.zh: 既然我们的故事始于那顿晚餐，你能告诉我你坐在谁旁边，你们聊了些什么吗？

sentences.en: And I was sitting next to Valadja Kailas Borak, a geophysicist, the world's leading authority in earthquake prediction.
sentences.zh: 当时我坐在瓦拉贾·凯拉斯·博拉克（Valadja Kailas Borak）旁边，他是一位地球物理学家，也是全球地震预测领域的权威。

sentences.en: And it was Kailas Borak who suggested that we should collaborate.
sentences.zh: 正是凯拉斯·博拉克建议我们应该合作。

sentences.en: And of course, being a prescient, foresightful scholar, my answer was, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 当然，作为一个有先见之明、深谋远虑的学者，我的回答是：绝对不行。

sentences.en: What does geophysics have to do with elections?
sentences.zh: 地球物理学和大选有什么关系？

sentences.en: And then I began to think about it a little bit.
sentences.zh: 后来我开始认真思考这个问题。

sentences.en: And everything we know about elections, we've derived from geophysics anyway.
sentences.zh: 反正我们对大选的所有了解，都是从地球物理学中推导出来的。

sentences.en: Tremors of political change, volcanic elections, political earthquakes.
sentences.zh: 政治变革的震动、火山爆发般的选举、政治地震。

sentences.en: So why not explicitly steal from geophysics?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么不直接借鉴地球物理学呢？

sentences.en: And what we did was, we reinterpreted elections in geophysical terMs.
sentences.zh: 于是我们所做的，就是用地球物理学的术语重新解读大选。

sentences.en: That is, not as Republican versus Democrat, liberal versus conservative, or Carter versus Reagan.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，不是共和党对阵民主党，自由派对阵保守派，或者卡特对阵里根。

sentences.en: But in earthquake terms, as stability, the party holding the White House keeps the White House.
sentences.zh: 而是用地震术语：稳定，即执政党保住白宫。

sentences.en: And upheaval, the party holding the White House is turned out of office.
sentences.zh: 以及动荡，即执政党被赶下台。

sentences.en: We'll talk in a moment about the specifics of the model you built.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会讨论你所建立模型的具体细节。

sentences.en: But to make things clear, what you're saying is that you said,
sentences.zh: 但为了把问题说清楚，你的意思是，你当时说：

sentences.en: let's look at every presidential election as a referendum on the party currently holding the White House.
sentences.zh: 让我们把每一次总统大选都看作是对当前执政党的一次公投。

sentences.en: Our thesis was that elections are primarily judgments on the strength and performance of the party holding the White House.
sentences.zh: 我们的论点是，选举主要是对执政党实力和表现的评判。

sentences.en: And all the twists and turns of the campaign, the ads, the speeches, the campaign tricks, the debates,
sentences.zh: 而竞选中的所有曲折、广告、演讲、竞选花招、辩论，

sentences.en: count for little or nothing on Election Day.
sentences.zh: 在选举日当天几乎毫无意义。

sentences.en: But of course, this was just a theory.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这仅仅是一个理论。

sentences.en: And to test our theory and to create a model, we examined every American presidential election,
sentences.zh: 为了验证我们的理论并创建一个模型，我们研究了美国历次总统大选，

sentences.en: from the election of Lincoln in 1860 to the election of Reagan in 1980.
sentences.zh: 从1860年林肯当选到1980年里根当选。

sentences.en: And from that examination, we came up with, indeed, the 13 keys to the White House.
sentences.zh: 通过那次研究，我们确实得出了“通往白宫的13把钥匙”。
这是一个非常简单的概念。

sentences.en: The 13 keys are true-false questions that can be answered prior to an upcoming election,
sentences.zh: 这13把钥匙是是非题，可以在即将到来的大选前回答，

sentences.en: sometimes years in advance if they fall into place.
sentences.zh: 如果条件成熟，有时甚至可以提前几年回答。

sentences.en: And an answer of true always favors the re-election of the party in power.
sentences.zh: 回答“是”总是利于执政党的连任。

sentences.en: An answer of false always predicts political upheaval the party in power will lose.
sentences.zh: 回答“否”总是预示着政治动荡，即执政党将会落败。

sentences.en: And the decision rule is really simple.
The party in power will lose if six or more of the 13 keys are false.
sentences.zh: 如果13把钥匙中有6把或以上为“否”，执政党就会落败。

sentences.en: That was the model we came up with in 1981.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在1981年提出的模型。

sentences.en: So what you did, Alan, is you looked at every election starting in 1860,
sentences.zh: 所以艾伦，你所做的是回顾了从1860年开始的每一次选举，

sentences.en: and you said, what are the factors that might have influenced this election?
sentences.zh: 然后你问，有哪些因素可能影响了这次选举？

sentences.en: And you used that to come up with this model of 13 keys.
sentences.zh: 并利用这些因素得出了这个13把钥匙的模型。

sentences.en: Tell us a little bit about these keys and these 13 questions.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲这些钥匙和这13个问题吧。

sentences.en: Yes, these 13 questions primarily gauge the strength and performance of the party
sentences.zh: 是的，这13个问题主要衡量的是执政党的实力和表现。

sentences.en: There are four political keys that have to do with midterm elections,
sentences.zh: 有四把政治钥匙与中期选举有关，

sentences.en: contests for the White House party presidential nomination,
sentences.zh: 与白宫党内总统提名竞争有关，

sentences.en: whether the sitting president is running or not, third parties.
sentences.zh: 与现任总统是否参选有关，以及第三方候选人。

sentences.en: Then there are a whole series of performance keys, short and long-term economy,
sentences.zh: 然后是一系列表现钥匙：短期和长期经济、

sentences.en: scandals, social unrest, policy change, foreign policy successes, and failures.
sentences.zh: 丑闻、社会动荡、政策变革、外交政策的成功与失败。

sentences.en: Only two keys relate to the candidates at all, and they're very high threshold keys.
sentences.zh: 只有两把钥匙与候选人有关，而且它们的门槛非常高。

sentences.en: They ask whether the candidate of the White House party is one of those once-in-a-generation
sentences.zh: 它们询问白宫党的候选人是否是那种一代人一遇的、

sentences.en: charismatic candidates like a Ronald Reagan or a John F.
sentences.zh: 像罗纳德·里根或约翰·F·肯尼迪那样具有个人魅力的候选人。

sentences.en: And then they ask whether the challenging party candidate is charismatic.
sentences.zh: 然后它们会询问挑战党的候选人是否具有个人魅力。

sentences.en: That is the only key, the 13th key, that has anything to do with the challengers.
sentences.zh: 这是唯一一把与挑战者有关的钥匙，即第13把钥匙。

sentences.en: So this is fascinating because, of course, when we think about presidential elections
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了，因为当然，当我们思考总统大选，

sentences.en: and we think of the way the media cover presidential elections,
sentences.zh: 当我们思考媒体报道总统大选的方式时，

sentences.en: we think it all comes down to the candidates, and we pay enormous attention.
sentences.zh: 我们认为一切都取决于候选人，我们给予了极大的关注。

sentences.en: And you would say that is actually inordinate attention.
sentences.zh: 而你会说，这种关注实际上是过度的。

sentences.en: I think the media covers elections as though they were horse races,
sentences.zh: 我认为媒体报道选举就像报道赛马一样，

sentences.en: with candidates sprinting ahead and falling behind,
sentences.zh: 候选人根据竞选的曲折起伏，

sentences.en: according to the twists and turns of the campaigns,

sentences.zh: 而民调专家则在记录比分。

sentences.en: But the whole point is that's not how elections really work.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，选举并不是那样运作的。

sentences.en: The American people are fundamentally pragmatic,
sentences.zh: 美国人民本质上是务实的，

sentences.en: and they are asking whether or not the White House party merits four more years of office.
sentences.zh: 他们是在问执政党是否值得再执政四年。

sentences.en: And it's the record of the four years, the keys go term by term,
sentences.zh: 真正重要的是这四年的记录，钥匙是按任期来算的，

sentences.en: that really counts, not all of these events of the campaign,
sentences.zh: 而不是竞选中的所有这些事件，

sentences.en: that the media spends hundreds of millions of dollars covering each election.
sentences.zh: 媒体在每次选举中花费数亿美元去报道这些事件。

sentences.en: And as a result, almost all of the media coverage is not only irrelevant,
sentences.zh: 结果就是，几乎所有的媒体报道不仅无关紧要，
而且在很大程度上具有误导性。

sentences.en: It sends listeners and viewers and readers down into blind alleys.
sentences.zh: 它把听众、观众和读者带入了死胡同。

sentences.en: It's not quite right to sort of say you are looking into a crystal ball.
sentences.zh: 说你在看水晶球并不完全准确。

sentences.en: What you've really done is you've said,
looking back historically at dozens of elections,
sentences.zh: 回顾历史上几十次选举，

sentences.en: what are the different factors that played a role in each of these elections?
sentences.zh: 在这些选举中，哪些不同的因素发挥了作用？

sentences.en: And you're saying history can be a guide when we look into the future.
sentences.zh: 而你是在说，当我们展望未来时，历史可以成为指南。

sentences.en: I don't look at crystal balls.
I don't have a pipeline to the Almighty.
sentences.zh: 我没有通往上帝的渠道。

sentences.en: And my system is guided by a deep study of history
sentences.zh: 我的系统是由对历史的深入研究指导的，

sentences.en: that covers a very broad span of time all the way back to 1860.
sentences.zh: 涵盖了从1860年至今的非常广泛的时间跨度。

sentences.en: And thus is an extremely robust system.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一个极其稳健的系统。

sentences.en: That is, it has survived enormous changes in our economy,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，它在我们的经济、社会、政治和技术发生巨大变化的情况下依然有效。

sentences.en: in our society, in our politics, in our technology.
sentences.zh: 在我们的社会、政治和技术方面。

sentences.en: We go all the way back to the horse and buggy days of American politics.
sentences.zh: 我们一直追溯到美国政治的马车时代。

sentences.en: And that's the beauty of looking at history
sentences.zh: 这就是研究历史并使用这种模式识别方法的魅力所在。

sentences.en: and using this pattern recognition methodology.

sentences.zh: 我们将探讨这个模型的一些非凡特征。

sentences.en: we're going to explore some of the extraordinary features of this model.
sentences.zh: 它让艾伦有时能在候选人宣布参选前很久就预测出选举结果。
